problem: The reasoning is thermodynamically wrong. It says that at a lower rejection temperature 'less entropy is carried away per unit of heat'. Entropy carried away per unit heat is Q/T, so a lower T means MORE entropy per unit heat, not less. The heat rejected also is not 'the same' — it falls. A student who memorises this sentence will get the second law backwards in the exam.
fix: It lowers the saturation temperature T_c at which heat is rejected. The cycle's entropy change at rejection, s₄ − s₁, is fixed by the other states, so q_out = T_c (s₄ − s₁) becomes smaller while turbine work stays about the same; net work rises for the same boiler heat, exactly as the Carnot argument predicts.

problem: The steady-flow balance q − w = Δh is written, then pump work is given as w_p = h₂ − h₁. For the pump (q = 0) this balance gives w = −(h₂ − h₁), so w_p as written is the work input magnitude, not w of the sign convention. A careful student may think the two statements contradict each other.
fix: Add one line: 'w_t and w_p are both taken as positive magnitudes — w_t is work delivered by the turbine, w_p is work absorbed by the pump. In the sign convention of q − w = Δh, the pump work is w = −w_p.'
